Other stories extend the header through plugin slots
A plain form post, checked on the server
Signing out is a link, not a script
One products file, copied from Swag Labs' own data
localStorage cart-contents is the cart, and every change is announced
Rendered on the server in name order
The id in the address picks the product
A select that reorders the list in place
Buttons and badge follow the cart store's events
Rendered in the browser from the cart store
Contributed to the shell, links where it can
Checked in the browser, in Swag Labs' order
Finish clears the cart before leaving
Check a part against Swag Labs' own e2e tests
Sign-in refusals are drawn in the browser, in the same click
Browser scripts are served at their source paths, and the cart drives every button and badge
Browser scripts import neighbours by their /assets address; tests map those addresses with a resolve hook
A story package's tests import its plugin statically
The overview is drawn in the browser from an embedded catalog, before load
Sign-up lives in its own package; who can sign in stays in Signing in
An order is a snapshot, priced by the server when it is placed
Admin edits the catalog through Browsing; it keeps no data of its own
Reviews plug into Browsing's pages; Browsing never imports Reviews
Each story keeps its own JSON file in one data folder, written atomically
products.json stays the starting catalog; stock and admin prices are a data file over it
The server keeps the checkout name and postal code between the two steps
/api/me is not a guarded page: it answers 401 instead of redirecting
The server filters by ?q=; the browser filters as you type and rewrites ?q=
The page shell draws the greeting from the request's user
Sign-up checks like sign-in: the same rules in the browser first, the server the authority
Finish becomes a form post; the cart is cleared on the complete page, not on the click
My Orders is a plain server-drawn list; the menu link is a static entry

Extras register in process at start-up
Someone else's order looks exactly like a missing one
headerHtml may be a function of the signed-in user
Drawn on the server, never hidden in the page
May review = has an order holding the product and no review of it yet
Rating wording is one shared function
Drawn by the server through Product extras
The form posts to the product page and comes back to it
Signed-up accounts use the bare session-username cookie too
The sign-in page's script knows signed-up users by username only

stories.title: Signing in
stories.description: A shopper signs in as a Swag Labs user, stays signed in through the session-username cookie, and signs out. Every page but the sign-in page needs them signed in.

capabilities.title: 1 · Shop server
capabilities.description: The node:http server behind npm start: listens on PORT (3000 by default), finds every story package's routes and browser scripts, and serves them.

contracts.title: 1.1 · listens on PORT, 3000 by default
contracts.description: npm start serves the shop at http://localhost:3000; setting PORT changes the port.

contracts.title: 1.2 · mounts every story package's plugin
contracts.description: Routes, scripts and assets exported by any packages/*/src/index.js are served without the server naming the package; unknown addresses get 404.

capabilities.title: 2 · Session
capabilities.description: Who is signed in: the session-username cookie, read on every request, and the guard that sends anyone not signed in to the sign-in page.

contracts.title: 2.1 · a valid session-username cookie signs the browser in
contracts.description: A request carrying session-username=standard_user (however it was set) reaches a guarded page.

reported.note: No genuine red: session.js was written with the Shop server, which needed it to guard routes; the test was written after and passes.

contracts.title: 2.2 · no valid session sends you to sign in
contracts.description: A guarded page with no cookie, an unknown username or locked_out_user redirects to /.

reported.note: No genuine red: session.js was written with the Shop server, which needed it to guard routes; the test was written after and passes.

capabilities.title: 3 · Page shell
capabilities.description: The frame of every signed-in page: the header with the .shopping_cart_link cart link (empty when the cart is empty), plus the header pieces and browser scripts other story packages contribute.

contracts.title: 3.1 · header has an empty cart link
contracts.description: Every signed-in page has a header with a .shopping_cart_link to /cart.html holding no text of its own.

reported.note: No genuine red: page-shell.js was written with the Shop server, which renders pages through it; test written after.

contracts.title: 3.2 · plugins' header pieces and scripts appear on every signed-in page
contracts.description: Header HTML and scripts a plugin contributes are included in every page the shell renders.

reported.note: No genuine red: page-shell.js was written with the Shop server; test written after.

capabilities.title: 4 · Sign-in page
capabilities.description: The page at / with #login_button_container, #user-name, #password and the .btn_action button; it signs standard_user in to Products and shows Swag Labs' exact errors in [data-test="error"].

contracts.title: 4.1 · sign-in page has Swag Labs' form
contracts.description: / shows #login_button_container holding #user-name, #password and a .btn_action button, with no required attributes.

contracts.title: 4.2 · standard_user signs in to Products
contracts.description: standard_user / secret_sauce sets session-username=standard_user and goes to /inventory.html.

contracts.title: 4.3 · refusals show Swag Labs' exact errors
contracts.description: [data-test="error"] reads 'Epic sadface: Sorry, this user has been locked out.', 'Epic sadface: Username is required', 'Epic sadface: Password is required' or 'Epic sadface: Username and password do not match any user in this service', and no cookie is set.

contracts.title: 4.4 · a refusal shows in the same click, without leaving the page
contracts.description: With the page's script running, submitting refused details shows the Swag Labs error in [data-test="error"] synchronously and sends nothing (Swag Labs' login.spec checks isDisplayed with no wait); accepted details still post, and the server stays the authority.

reported.note: Also checked in Edge with Swag Labs' login.spec against a server delaying POSTs 400ms: 5/5 pass, and the locked user sent no POST.

capabilities.title: 5 · Sign-out
capabilities.description: GET /logout clears the session-username cookie and sends the shopper to the sign-in page; the side menu's Logout link points here.

contracts.title: 5.1 · signing out clears the cookie and returns to sign in
contracts.description: GET /logout expires session-username on path / and redirects to /; Products then redirects to / again.

capabilities.title: 6 · Accounts store
capabilities.description: Who can sign in: Swag Labs' users from users.json, plus accounts made by signing up (full name, username, hashed password) kept in accounts.json in the shop's data folder, plus admin_user. Gives each user's display name.

contracts.title: 6.1 · an account made by signing up can sign in, and survives a restart
contracts.description: createAccount({name, username, password}) writes accounts.json in SHOP_DATA_DIR; a new server reading the same folder finds the user and accepts the password.

contracts.title: 6.2 · passwords are stored hashed and never sent to the browser
contracts.description: accounts.json holds no password in clear; the sign-in page embeds only Swag Labs' users (as it does today), never signed-up accounts or admin_user.

contracts.title: 6.3 · admin_user signs in with secret_sauce, unlisted
contracts.description: admin_user / secret_sauce signs in to Products; it is not in the sign-in page's 'Accepted usernames' list; its name, like Swag Labs' users', is its username.

contracts.title: 6.4 · a signed-up user signs in with the sign-in page; Swag Labs' refusals still show in the same click
contracts.description: The sign-in page's script refuses in the same click only what it can know (empty fields, Swag Labs' users); any other username posts and the server answers, with the same Epic sadface messages. Swag Labs' login.spec still passes.

capabilities.title: 7 · Greeting
capabilities.description: Every signed-in page's header shows [data-test="greeting"] reading "Hi, <full name>" (the username for Swag Labs' users and admin_user).

contracts.title: 7.1 · every signed-in page greets the user by name
contracts.description: [data-test="greeting"] reads 'Hi, Ada Lovelace' for a signed-up Ada Lovelace and 'Hi, standard_user' for standard_user, on Products, Cart, Checkout and every other signed-in page; the sign-in page has none.

capabilities.title: 8 · Per-user header pieces
capabilities.description: A plugin's header piece may depend on who is signed in, and plugins may contribute side-menu links shown only to some users.

contracts.title: 8.1 · header pieces and menu links can depend on who is signed in
contracts.description: A plugin's headerHtml given as a function receives the signed-in user; a menuLinks entry with show(user) is drawn in the side menu only when it answers true. String headerHtml works as before.

stories.title: Browsing

contracts.title: 1.1 · six products with Swag Labs' ids, names, descriptions and prices
contracts.description: Ids 0 to 5 match the requirements and Swag Labs' InventoryData.js exactly; prices format as $29.99.

capabilities.title: 2 · Cart store
capabilities.description: The one browser module that reads and changes the cart in localStorage cart-contents (a JSON array of product ids) and announces each change, used by the badge, the buttons, the Cart page, the menu and Checkout.

contracts.title: 2.1 · reads cart-contents as a list of product ids
contracts.description: '[4]' reads as [4]; missing or malformed contents read as an empty cart.

contracts.title: 2.2 · add, remove and clear write cart-contents and announce cart-changed
contracts.description: Each change writes the JSON array back (no duplicates) and fires a cart-changed event.

capabilities.title: 3 · Products page
capabilities.description: /inventory.html for signed-in shoppers: .inventory_list with one .inventory_item per product (.inventory_item_name, .inventory_item_desc, .inventory_item_price), name A to Z by default.

contracts.title: 3.1 · lists the six products A to Z
contracts.description: /inventory.html has .inventory_list with six .inventory_item, Sauce Labs Backpack first and Test.allTheThings() T-Shirt (Red) last.

contracts.title: 3.2 · each item shows its name, description and price
contracts.description: Each .inventory_item has .inventory_item_name, .inventory_item_desc and .inventory_item_price ('$29.99').

capabilities.description: /inventory-item.html?id=N: .inventory_details with .inventory_details_name, _desc, _price and a .inventory_details_back_button to Products; each product name on Products links here.

contracts.title: 4.1 · shows the product named by ?id=
contracts.description: /inventory-item.html?id=4 has .inventory_details with .inventory_details_name 'Sauce Labs Backpack', its .inventory_details_desc and .inventory_details_price '$29.99'; an unknown id gets a not-found page.

reported.note: Names sit inside a#item_<id>_title_link; the back button is a submit button in a GET form to /inventory.html, so it works without scripts.

capabilities.title: 5 · Sorting
capabilities.description: The .product_sort_container menu on Products: name A to Z, name Z to A, price low to high, price high to low.

contracts.title: 5.1 · sort menu offers the four orders
contracts.description: .product_sort_container offers name A to Z (selected), name Z to A, price low to high, price high to low.

contracts.title: 5.2 · each choice reorders the products
contracts.description: Choosing an order puts the .inventory_item elements in that order (ties in price keep name order).

reported.note: Reorders in place in the change event; the server sorts with the same function, so name order agrees.

capabilities.title: 6 · Cart buttons and badge
capabilities.description: Add to cart (btn_primary btn_inventory) / Remove (btn_secondary btn_inventory) on Products and the product page, and the .shopping_cart_badge count inside the header's cart link on every signed-in page.

contracts.title: 6.1 · Add to cart and Remove swap on Products and the product page
contracts.description: A product not in the cart shows Add to cart (btn_primary btn_inventory); clicking adds it and shows Remove (btn_secondary btn_inventory); clicking Remove takes it out. Both pages read cart-contents set beforehand.

reported.note: Also in headless Edge: Swag Labs' swag.items.list add/remove and swag.item.details add/remove pass.

contracts.title: 6.2 · the badge counts the cart, and is gone when empty
contracts.description: On every signed-in page .shopping_cart_link's text is the number of products ('1') and empty when the cart is empty, updating straight away on cart-changed.

reported.note: Also in headless Edge: getCartAmount reads '' and '1' as Swag Labs' specs expect; also redraws on the storage event from other tabs.

capabilities.title: 7 · Stock and prices
capabilities.description: Each product's stock (10 to start) and its current price, kept as changes over products.json in the data folder; the stock label on Products and the product page, Add to cart disabled when sold out, and takeStock for Finish.

contracts.title: 7.1 · every product starts with 10; set price and stock survive a restart
contracts.description: With an empty data folder each product has stock 10 and its products.json price; setProduct(id, {price, stock}) writes catalog.json and a restarted server reads the same values; products.json is never written.

contracts.title: 7.2 · the stock label reads In stock, Only n left or Sold out

contracts.title: 7.3 · a sold-out product's Add to cart is disabled
contracts.description: At stock 0 the Add to cart button on Products and the product page has disabled; a sold-out product already in the cart still shows an enabled Remove.

contracts.description: takeStock([4, 0]) lowers each by one and saves; if any is at 0 it changes nothing and answers that product (the first sold-out one in cart order).

contracts.title: 8.1 · typing filters names and descriptions as you type, ignoring case
contracts.description: Typing 'BACKPACK' into [data-test="search"] leaves only Sauce Labs Backpack as .inventory_item, with no reload; a word found only in a description matches too; clearing the box brings all six back.

reported.note: search.test.js 8.1 passes; also checked in headless Edge

contracts.title: 8.2 · the address keeps the search
contracts.description: Typing updates the address to /inventory.html?q=backpack (no q when empty); opening or reloading that address shows the box filled and the list already filtered.

reported.note: search.test.js 8.2 passes; reload of ?q=backpack checked in headless Edge

contracts.title: 8.3 · no match says so, with no items in the page
contracts.description: [data-test="no-results"] reads 'No products match “zzz”.' (curly quotes, what was typed) and the page holds no .inventory_item, whether typed or opened from ?q=zzz.

reported.note: search.test.js 8.3 passes, including working buttons on put-back items

contracts.title: 8.4 · sorting works on the filtered list
contracts.description: The sort options keep the values az, za, lohi, hilo; sorting while searching orders only the matches, and changing the search keeps the chosen order.

reported.note: search.test.js 8.4 passes

capabilities.title: 9 · Product extras

fields.title: Can someone pretend to be another shopper with the cookie?
fields.answer: Leave the cookie as it is: it's a test shop, so trusting it is fine.
fields.stakes: Whether one shopper can see another's orders and post reviews in their name. Changing it later means everyone signed in is signed out once.
fields.context: Today the shop trusts whatever username is in the session-username cookie, because Swag Labs' tests sign in by setting that cookie by hand. So anyone can type a cookie and become any user. That doesn't matter for Swag Labs' demo users, but with real accounts it would let one person open another's orders (Part 6) and write reviews as them (Part 8). Your requirements say the browser keeps only that cookie, so a signature would go inside its value (e.g. 'ada.k3J9…'), not in a new cookie. admin_user's password is the public secret_sauce, so signing doesn't protect the admin either way.
fields.options:
A) Sign it for accounts made by signing up; Swag Labs' users (and admin_user) still work with the bare username, so Swag Labs' tests are unaffected. Your own tests must sign up or sign in through the pages, not set the cookie by hand for new accounts, and shouldn't expect the cookie to equal the username.
B) Leave it bare for everyone, exactly like Swag Labs: simplest, but anyone can be anyone.
fields.statement: For accounts made by signing up, should the session-username cookie carry a server signature so it can't be faked, or stay the bare username as Swag Labs does?
fields.recommendation: A: it keeps every Swag Labs test working and makes 'Another user's order shows Order not found' mean something.

A) Split: the first half now with 5 and 6; the second half (small) afterwards, as a third session beside Parts 7 and 8, or by whichever first-wave session is free first.
B) Keep Part 9 whole in the first wave: its session builds the first half, then waits for Parts 5 and 6 to merge before finishing.
